passages.text: During the reign of David there was a famine for three successive years, and David sought the face of the LORD. And the LORD said, “It is because of the blood shed by Saul and his family, because he killed the Gibeonites.”
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
A famine happened during David’s reign.
The famine lasted three years in a row.
David wanted to know why the famine came.
David prayed to the LORD.
The LORD answered David.
The LORD said Saul and his family killed the Gibeonites.
The LORD said Saul’s actions brought bloodshed.
The LORD said the famine happened because of this bloodshed.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י רָעָב֩ בִּימֵ֨י דָוִ֜ד שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים שָׁנָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁנָ֔ה וַיְבַקֵּ֥שׁ דָּוִ֖ד אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑הס וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־ שָׁאוּל֙ וְאֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הַדָּמִ֔ים עַל־ אֲשֶׁר־ הֵמִ֖ית אֶת־ הַגִּבְעֹנִֽים׃

passages.text: At this, David summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites, but a remnant of the Amorites. The Israelites had taken an oath concerning them, but in his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul had sought to kill them.)
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
David called the Gibeonites.
David spoke to the Gibeonites.
The Gibeonites were not Israelites.
The Gibeonites were a remnant of the Amorites.
The Israelites had made an oath to the Gibeonites.
Saul was king before David.
Saul was very zealous for Israel and Judah.
Saul tried to kill the Gibeonites.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לַגִּבְעֹנִ֖ים וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְהַגִּבְעֹנִ֞ים לֹ֣א מִבְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֚י אִם־ מִיֶּ֣תֶר הָאֱמֹרִ֔י וּבְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נִשְׁבְּע֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם וַיְבַקֵּ֤שׁ שָׁאוּל֙ לְהַכֹּתָ֔ם בְּקַנֹּאת֥וֹ לִבְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִיהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: So David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How can I make amends so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to the Gibeonites.
The Gibeonites were not Israelites.
David said, “What shall I do for you?”
David asked, “How can I make amends?”
David wanted the Gibeonites to bless the inheritance of the LORD.
The inheritance of the LORD means the people of Israel.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־ הַגִּבְעֹנִ֔ים מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לָכֶ֑ם וּבַמָּ֣ה אֲכַפֵּ֔ר וּבָרְכ֖וּ אֶת־ נַחֲלַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The Gibeonites said to him, “We need no silver or gold from Saul or his house, nor should you put to death anyone in Israel for us.” “Whatever you ask, I will do for you,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
The Gibeonites spoke to David.
The Gibeonites said, “We do not want silver or gold from Saul or his house.
We do not want anyone in Israel to be put to death for us.”
David replied, “I will do whatever you say.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ הַגִּבְעֹנִ֗ים אֵֽין־ לִי כֶּ֤סֶף וְזָהָב֙ עִם־ שָׁא֣וּל וְעִם־ בֵּית֔וֹ וְאֵֽין־ לָ֥נוּ אִ֖ישׁ לְהָמִ֣ית בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מָֽה־ אַתֶּ֥ם אֹמְרִ֖ים אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And they answered the king, “As for the man who consumed us and plotted against us to exterminate us from existing within any border of Israel, let seven of his male descendants be delivered to us so that we may hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.” “I will give them to you,” said the king.
passages.sermon:
The Gibeonites spoke to King David.
They said, “Saul tried to destroy us.
He planned to wipe us out.
He wanted us gone from all the land of Israel.
Give us seven of Saul’s male descendants.
We will hang them before the LORD.
We will do this at Gibeah of Saul.
Gibeah is the place the LORD chose.
The king said, “I will give them to you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּלָּ֔נוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּמָּה־ לָ֑נוּ נִשְׁמַ֕דְנוּ מֵֽהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב בְּכָל־ גְּבֻ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ יְנָתָן לָ֜נוּ שִׁבְעָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מִבָּנָ֔יו וְהוֹקַֽעֲנוּם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּגִבְעַ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל בְּחִ֣יר יְהוָ֑הס וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲנִ֥י אֶתֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Now the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
passages.sermon:
The king was David.
David spared Mephibosheth.
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan.
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
David spared Mephibosheth because of an oath.
David and Jonathan made this oath before the LORD.
passages.original: וַיַּחְמֹ֣ל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַל־ מְפִי־ בֹ֖שֶׁת בֶּן־ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בֶּן־ שָׁא֑וּל עַל־ שְׁבֻעַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּֽינֹתָ֔ם בֵּ֣ין דָּוִ֔ד וּבֵ֖ין יְהוֹנָתָ֥ן בֶּן־ שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons whom Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul, as well as the five sons whom Merab daughter of Saul had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
passages.sermon:
The king acted.
The king took Armoni and Mephibosheth.
Armoni and Mephibosheth were sons of Rizpah.
Rizpah was the daughter of Aiah.
Rizpah had borne these sons to Saul.
The king also took five sons of Merab.
Merab was the daughter of Saul.
Merab had borne these five sons to Adriel.
Adriel was the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ אֶת־ שְׁ֠נֵי בְּנֵ֨י רִצְפָּ֤ה בַת־ אַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלְדָ֣ה לְשָׁא֔וּל אֶת־ אַרְמֹנִ֖י וְאֶת־ מְפִבֹ֑שֶׁת וְאֶת־ חֲמֵ֗שֶׁת בְּנֵי֙ מִיכַ֣ל בַּת־ שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלְדָ֛ה לְעַדְרִיאֵ֥ל בֶּן־ בַּרְזִלַּ֖י הַמְּחֹלָתִֽי׃

passages.text: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before the LORD. So all seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
passages.sermon:
King David gave seven men to the Gibeonites.
The Gibeonites took the seven men.
The Gibeonites hanged the seven men on a hill.
The hill was before the LORD.
All seven men died together.
They died at the start of the harvest.
This was the beginning of the barley harvest.
passages.original: וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֞ם בְּיַ֣ד הַגִּבְעֹנִ֗ים וַיֹּקִיעֻ֤ם בָּהָר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְּל֥וּ שִׁבְעָתַיִם יָ֑חַד וְהֵם הֻמְת֜וּ בִּימֵ֤י קָצִיר֙ בָּרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים תְּחִלַּת קְצִ֥יר שְׂעֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven poured down on the bodies, she did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
passages.sermon:
Rizpah was the daughter of Aiah.
She was also a concubine of Saul.
Rizpah took sackcloth.
She spread the sackcloth for herself on a rock.
She did this at the beginning of the harvest.
She stayed there until rain from heaven fell on the bodies.
Rizpah did not allow the birds of the air to rest on the bodies during the day.
She did not allow the beasts of the field to come near the bodies at night.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֣ח רִצְפָּה֩ בַת־ אַיָּ֨ה אֶת־ הַשַּׂ֜ק וַתַּטֵּ֨הוּ לָ֤הּ אֶל־ הַצּוּר֙ מִתְּחִלַּ֣ת קָצִ֔יר עַ֛ד נִתַּךְ־ מַ֥יִם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִן־ הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְלֹֽא־ נָתְנָה֩ ע֨וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם לָנ֤וּחַ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְאֶת־ חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לָֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: When David was told what Saul’s concubine Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, had done, he went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan where the Philistines had hung the bodies after they had struck down Saul at Gilboa.
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
Rizpah was the daughter of Aiah.
Rizpah was Saul’s concubine.
Someone told David what Rizpah had done.
David heard about Rizpah’s actions.
David went to the men of Jabesh-gilead.
The men of Jabesh-gilead had taken the bones of Saul and Jonathan.
Saul was the former king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
The men of Jabesh-gilead had stolen the bones from the public square of Beth-shan.
The Philistines had hung the bodies of Saul and Jonathan in Beth-shan.
The Philistines had killed Saul at Gilboa.
David took the bones of Saul and Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לְדָוִ֑ד אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשְׂתָ֛ה רִצְפָּ֥ה בַת־ אַיָּ֖ה פִּלֶ֥גֶשׁ שָׁאֽוּל׃ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־ עַצְמ֤וֹת שָׁאוּל֙ וְאֶת־ עַצְמוֹת֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֔וֹ מֵאֵ֕ת בַּעֲלֵ֖י יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד אֲשֶׁר֩ גָּנְב֨וּ אֹתָ֜ם מֵרְחֹ֣ב בֵּֽית־ שַׁ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר תָּלוּם שָׁם הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים בְּי֨וֹם הַכּ֧וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אֶת־ שָׁא֖וּל בַּגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

passages.text: So David had the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan brought from there, along with the bones of those who had been hanged.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David gave an order.
Men brought the bones of Saul from Jabesh-gilead.
Saul was the former king of Israel.
They also brought the bones of Jonathan.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
They gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַל מִשָּׁם֙ אֶת־ עַצְמ֣וֹת שָׁא֔וּל וְאֶת־ עַצְמ֖וֹת יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֑וֹ וַיַּ֣אַסְפ֔וּ אֶת־ עַצְמ֖וֹת הַמּוּקָעִֽים׃

passages.text: And they buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Zela in the land of Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. After they had done everything the king had commanded, God answered their prayers for the land.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the former king of Israel.
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
The people took the bones of Saul and Jonathan.
They buried the bones in Zela.
Zela is in the land of Benjamin.
They placed the bones in the tomb of Kish.
Kish was Saul’s father.
The people did everything the king commanded.
After this, God answered the prayers for the land.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֶת־ עַצְמוֹת־ שָׁא֣וּל וִיהוֹנָֽתָן־ בְּ֠נוֹ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ בִּנְיָמִ֜ן בְּצֵלָ֗ע בְּקֶ֙בֶר֙ קִ֣ישׁ אָבִ֔יו וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּעָתֵ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים לָאָ֖רֶץ אַֽחֲרֵי־ כֵֽן׃פ

passages.text: Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines; but David became exhausted.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines started another war against Israel.
David was the king of Israel.
David went down to the battle.
David’s servants went with him.
David and his servants fought against the Philistines.
David became very tired.
passages.original: וַתְּהִי־ ע֧וֹד מִלְחָמָ֛ה לַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֨רֶד דָּוִ֜ד וַעֲבָדָ֥יו עִמּ֛וֹ וַיִּלָּחֲמ֥וּ אֶת־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וַיָּ֥עַף דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: Then Ishbi-benob, a descendant of Rapha, whose bronze spear weighed three hundred shekels and who was bearing a new sword, resolved to kill David.
passages.sermon:
Ishbi-benob was a descendant of Rapha.
He carried a bronze spear.
His spear weighed three hundred shekels.
He wore a new sword.
Ishbi-benob decided to kill David.
passages.original: וְיִשְׁבּוֹ בְּנֹ֜ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ בִּילִידֵ֣י הָרָפָ֗ה וּמִשְׁקַ֤ל קֵינוֹ֙ שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְה֖וּא חָג֣וּר חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת־ דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him, “You must never again go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.”
passages.sermon:
Abishai was the son of Zeruiah.
Abishai saw that David was in danger.
Abishai came to help David.
Abishai struck the Philistine.
Abishai killed the Philistine.
David’s men saw what happened.
David’s men made a promise to David.
They said, “You must not go out to battle with us again.”
They said, “We do not want the lamp of Israel to be put out.”
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲזָר־ לוֹ֙ אֲבִישַׁ֣י בֶּן־ צְרוּיָ֔ה וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ אָ֣ז נִשְׁבְּעוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁי־ דָוִ֨ד ל֜וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹא־ תֵצֵ֨א ע֤וֹד אִתָּ֙נוּ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תְכַבֶּ֖ה אֶת־ נֵ֥ר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Some time later at Gob, there was another battle with the Philistines. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha.
passages.sermon:
Sibbecai was a Hushathite.
Sibbecai was a servant of David.
Saph was a descendant of Rapha.
Saph was a Philistine.
Some time later, there was another battle at Gob.
The Philistines fought against Israel at Gob.
During this battle, Sibbecai killed Saph.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־ כֵ֔ן וַתְּהִי־ ע֧וֹד הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה בְּג֖וֹב עִם־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים אָ֣ז הִכָּ֗ה סִבְּכַי֙ הַחֻ֣שָׁתִ֔י אֶת־ סַ֕ף אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּילִדֵ֥י הָרָפָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
passages.sermon:
There was another battle at Gob.
The Philistines fought in this battle.
Elhanan fought in this battle.
Elhanan was the son of Jair.
Elhanan was from Bethlehem.
Goliath the Gittite was in this battle.
Goliath’s spear had a shaft like a weaver’s beam.
Elhanan killed Goliath the Gittite.
passages.original: וַתְּהִי־ ע֧וֹד הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה בְּג֖וֹב עִם־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּ֡ךְ אֶלְחָנָן֩ בֶּן־ יַעְרֵ֨י אֹרְגִ֜ים בֵּ֣ית הַלַּחְמִ֗י אֵ֚ת גָּלְיָ֣ת הַגִּתִּ֔י וְעֵ֣ץ חֲנִית֔וֹ כִּמְנ֖וֹר אֹרְגִֽים׃ס

passages.text: And there was still another battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha, and when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David’s brother Shimei killed him.
passages.sermon:
There was another battle at Gath.
A man of great size was there.
He had six fingers on each hand.
He had six toes on each foot.
He had twenty-four fingers and toes in total.
He was also a descendant of Rapha.
He taunted Israel.
Jonathan killed him.
Jonathan was the son of Shimei.
Shimei was David’s brother.
passages.original: וַתְּהִי־ ע֥וֹד מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּגַ֑ת וַיְהִ֣י׀ אִ֣ישׁ מָדִין וְאֶצְבְּעֹ֣ת יָדָיו֩ וְאֶצְבְּעֹ֨ת רַגְלָ֜יו שֵׁ֣שׁ וָשֵׁ֗שׁ עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְאַרְבַּע֙ מִסְפָּ֔ר וְגַם־ ה֖וּא יֻלַּ֥ד לְהָרָפָֽה׃ וַיְחָרֵ֖ף אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּכֵּ֙הוּ֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן בֶּן־ שִׁמְעִי אֲחִ֥י דָוִֽד׃

passages.text: So these four descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants.
passages.sermon:
Four men were born to Rapha in Gath.
These four men fought against Israel.
David and his servants defeated them.
David and his servants killed these four men.
passages.original: אֶת־ אַרְבַּ֥עַת אֵ֛לֶּה יֻלְּד֥וּ לְהָרָפָ֖ה בְּגַ֑ת וַיִּפְּל֥וּ בְיַד־ דָּוִ֖ד וּבְיַ֥ד עֲבָדָֽיו׃פ
